prior_block:
PRICE PRIORS for recurring line types (statistical model fitted on the thresholds t revealed
in earlier games; gross amounts). How to use them:
- The amounts are final thresholds as they were revealed: they already contain whatever
  deductible, VAT and customary-price judgement applied in those cases, and they were computed
  from the full invoiced quantity (the whole quantity was indemnified there). For an
  indemnified line of this type take the stated amount for the line as t as it stands and give
  a price_log_sd that matches the stated range. Do not deduct a deductible from it and do not
  cut the invoiced quantity.
- Deviate only for something this case has and those cases did not: an aggregate cap or
  sub-limit that the lines of this invoice must share, a percentage reduction for a breached
  duty, or a purchase price or sum insured stated in the claim that limits the line.
- Whether a line is indemnified in THIS case is decided by the policy and the claim, not by
  the history. The history only says how often this line type was paid at all. A line type
  that was never indemnified before is usually an ancillary charge the policies do not carry;
  treat it as indemnified only if this policy clearly says so.
- line 2 "Hole drilling": indemnified in 1 of 3 earlier cases, t = 0 in 2; when indemnified t per pc about 70 (80% range 52 to 107); revealed per pc: >=64 (case 14)
- line 8 "Vehicle costs": indemnified in 16 of 32 earlier cases, t = 0 in 16; when indemnified t per pc about 80 (80% range 73 to 88); revealed per pc: >=83 (case 34), >=76 (case 34), >=65 (case 39), >=71 (case 40), >=82 (case 43), >=81 (case 44)
- line 9 "Skilled worker hours": indemnified in 3 of 7 earlier cases, t = 0 in 4; when indemnified t per hr about 43 (80% range 33 to 59); revealed per hr: 35-42 (case 24), 35-40 (case 26), 50-58 (case 36), so this line (14 hr) about 599 (458 to 821)
- line 12 "Removal and disposal of damaged insulation": indemnified in the one earlier case; when indemnified t per pc about 74 (80% range 55 to 113); revealed per pc: >=68 (case 21)
- line 19 "Rock wool pipe insulation": indemnified in all 3 earlier cases; when indemnified t per m about 22 (80% range 18.3 to 26); revealed per m: >=22 (case 39), >=19.4 (case 40), >=19.0 (case 44)
- line 20 "Construction waste disposal": indemnified in all 4 earlier cases; when indemnified t per unit about 60 (80% range 55 to 66); revealed per unit: >=57 (case 18), 58-61 (case 40), >=58 (case 43), >=57 (case 44)

items.rationale: Repair of tiled panel in the damage area is reinstatement to same kind and quality (policy 1.1, 7.1.1(b), 7.1.5, 7.1.6). Only the affected area is covered, and the photo/description confirm this is the panel removed due to water damage.
Drilling a hole through a new tile for the pipe is necessary for reinstatement of the damaged panel (policy 7.1.5, 7.1.6). Reference price prior: about 70 (range 52–107).
Material for reinstating the tiled panel in the damage area, same kind and quality as before (policy 7.1.6, 3.5(a)). Covered as part of the repair.
Levelling material for rebuilding the patch of render that was soft/damaged by water (policy 7.1.5, 7.1.6). Only the area behind the tiles is covered.
No such tile size exists; likely a mis-entry or unrelated to the actual reinstatement. Not covered unless proven necessary for the repair (policy 7.1.5, 3.5(e)).
Silicone joints in the internal corners of the tiled panel are necessary for reinstatement (policy 7.1.6). Only the affected area is covered.
Premium grade is not required; only standard-grade equivalent is indemnified (policy 3.5(a), 7.1.6). If used for the same joints as above, duplication is excluded (policy 3.5(d)).
Travel/call-out charge for the contractor, reimbursed once per document (policy 7.4.2). Reference prior: about 80 (range 73–88).
Labour for reinstatement in the damage area is covered at local rates (policy 7.4.1). Reference prior: about 599 (range 458–821) for 14 hrs.

items.description: Clean wall tile covering 1 flat rate
items.rationale: Cleaning of reinstated surfaces in the damage area is part of the repair (policy 3.5(c)). Covered if not duplicated elsewhere.
Removal of wet plasterboard boxing next to the damage area is covered if it was affected by the leak (policy 7.1.5, 7.1.6). Description confirms water damage.

items.description: Removal and disposal of damaged insulation 1 pcs
items.rationale: Removal and disposal of sodden mineral wool from the boxing is necessary due to water damage (policy 7.1.5, 5.2.1). Reference prior: about 74 (range 55–113).

items.description: Remove damp plaster in basement rooms 3 m²
items.rationale: Removal of damp render behind the tiled panel is necessary for reinstatement (policy 7.1.5, 7.1.6). Only the affected area is covered.

items.description: Remove damp plaster in attic 1 pcs
items.rationale: Attic gable plaster is unrelated to the insured event (pre-existing staining, not affected by this leak). Excluded (policy 3.5(b), 7.1.5).
Replacement of the chrome cover ring (wall rosette) broken during leak repair is necessary for reinstatement (policy 7.1.5, 7.1.6).
Disassembly/reassembly of pipework or fittings to access and repair the leak is covered as opening up and making good (policy 5.2.6, 7.1.5).
Drying of the affected area is covered as technical drying (policy 5.2.7, 7.1.5). Reference prior: about 403 for a flat rate, but this is for 7 days (likely less). Estimate pro-rata.
Flat-rate surcharges are only covered if attributable to necessary materials/services (policy 7.4.4). If not itemized, usually excluded.
Replacement of sodden lagging on the pipe is necessary for reinstatement (policy 7.1.5, 7.1.6). Reference prior: about 22 per m (range 18.3–26).
Disposal of debris from the repair is covered as debris removal (policy 5.2.1, 7.1.5). Reference prior: about 60 (range 55–66).
